rationale.a: 18 TR is adequate; solar gain factor is already embedded in 500 BTU/hr per m² commercial estimate.

rationale.correct: Step 1: Base load = 400 m² × 500 BTU/hr per m² = 200,000 BTU/hr = 16.7 TR (1 TR = 12,000 BTU/hr). Step 2: Solar gain adjustment = +30% = 16.7 TR × 1.30 = 21.7 TR design load. Step 3: PD 1058 recommends 10–20% oversizing allowance for part-load efficiency and future expansion. At lower end (10%), specify 21.7 × 1.10 = 23.9 TR ≈ 24 TR recommended. Step 4: Evaluation: 18 TR is UNDERSIZED by 5.9 TR (25% shortfall vs. 24 TR recommendation). Result: Inadequate system; will struggle in peak summer (35°C+ outdoors), cycling continuously, poor dehumidification in high-humidity periods. Recommend upgrading to 25–30 TR split-type (two 12.5–15 TR units) or single 24 TR VRF outdoor unit. Source: ALE-UTIL-002-04 quick estimate + solar adjustment; PD 1058 Section 3.2 oversizing guidance.
rationale.takeaway: South-facing buildings in tropical climate require explicit solar gain adjustment (+20–40% per ASHRAE solar load tables); combined with PD 1058 oversizing (10–20%), total adjustment can reach 40–60% above quick-estimate base, significantly affecting system selection—undersizing by 20–25% is common design error leading to inadequate cooling and humidity control.
